newsitem.title: UK: Russia mark Eurobond mandate due in Feb -dealers.
newsitem.headline: Russia mark Eurobond mandate due in Feb -dealers.

text.p: Russia was likely to award a mandate for a debut mark Eurobond by early February, syndicate managers said on Thursday.
"Russia is expected to appoint lead managers in a couple of weeks, around early February," a new issues trader at a European bank said.
Dealers said Credit Suisse First Boston and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell were frontrunners for the mandate, but officials there declined to comment.

Russia was expected to launch a deal for up to 1.0 billion marks by the end of the first quarter. Although a five-year maturity had been mooted before, dealers said Russia might opt for a longer-dated deal, perhaps at 10 years.
"The maturity will have to reflect where demand is for high-yielding mark paper, and that is at longer maturities," said a U.S. bank trader.
Traders pointed to Argentina's success in launching long-dated mark Eurobonds in 1996.
"Last March, Argentina issued a 10-year mark bond, and this was considered quite an achievement," said a Frankfurt-based syndicate manager.
"By the end of the year they launched a 30-year bond, and this sold like hot cakes. The Argentina example clearly shows where demand is," he said.
